sector_model: Cloud infrastructure software and services: revenue growth and ARR, gross margin after data centre depreciation, FCF after capex and capitalised software, finance lease obligations, SBC and dilution; P/E unreliable while tax and debt items distort GAAP income.
thesis: DigitalOcean Holdings (NYSE: DOCN), self-service cloud for developers and small businesses, now selling AI GPU capacity. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-03) read. Q3 revenue 321.2M vs 229.6M (+39.9%); 9M 860.3M vs 659.0M (+30.5%); ARR 1,285M vs 919M; AI Customer ARR 376M vs 97M; top 25 customers 27% of revenue vs 11%. Gross margin Q3 50.1% vs 59.6% and operating income Q3 33.0M vs 44.9M as depreciation and data centre cost grow (9M D&A 171.8M vs 97.0M). GAAP net income is distorted: 9M 2026 8.6M including a 57.1M induced conversion expense; 9M 2025 233.6M included a 59.5M tax benefit from a valuation allowance release and a 48.1M debt gain. TTM revenue 1,102.7M (901.4-659.0+860.3); TTM NI 34.3M (259.3-233.6+8.6, not meaningful); TTM operating income 137.8M; TTM OCF 375.4M (309.6-252.3+318.1); TTM PP&E capex 131.3M plus capitalised software 23.5M gives FCF 220.6M; equipment acquired under financing arrangements 75.1M in 9M 2026 (27.6M in 9M 2025) is extra spending funded by lease debt and is not in that FCF (FY2025 amount not located). TTM SBC 111.3M (own sum), so FCF after SBC is about 109M. Close 66.76 (2026-11-20, two sources agree; -13.4% that day, -22.7% from 86.32 on 11-13, cause not found) x 117,996,815 shares (cover, 2026-10-29) = 7.88B = 7.1x TTM revenue, 35.7x TTM FCF (FCF yield 2.8%, about 1.4% after SBC). Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 666.1M plus marketable securities 178.6M; debt 461.6M (312.1M current, 149.6M long term); finance lease and equipment financing obligations 923.6M (204.8M current); operating lease liabilities 666.6M; equity 1,416.5M after a March 2026 follow-on offering (887.9M proceeds) and the induced conversion of 2030 convertible notes into about 12.5M shares (dilution: shares 91.9M to 118.0M in nine months). Rapid growth is real but earnings power is unproven: margin fell, spending and leases rose, and the price is not cheap on cash flow.
counterthesis: Growth is being bought with capital: gross margin down about 9.5 points, equipment financing and finance leases of 924M, 27% of revenue from 25 customers (up from 11%, AI capacity customers may be less sticky), share count up 28% since December 2025, GAAP earnings noise hides thin owner earnings (FCF after SBC about 1.4% yield). The 13% drop on 11-20 is unexplained in sources read; if it reflects AI customer news, the growth driver could be at risk.
invalidation: Upgrade to deeper study only if gross margin stabilises near 50% with revenue growth above 25%, FCF after leases and SBC turns clearly positive, and AI ARR concentration is explained. Avoid if the top customer group is shown to be one or two contract renewals at lower prices, or if financing obligations keep rising faster than operating cash flow.
